Before / after

From weak reporting patterns to trusted operating models.

Before

DataMart design driven by source-system convenience and technical table structures.

After

DataMart design anchored in decision moments, business questions and trusted semantic outputs.

This article expands the LinkedIn presentation into a practical framework for People Analytics leaders, practitioners and data teams. It focuses on the choices that make workforce information trusted, explainable and decision-ready.

01 · Deep dive

Decision → Question → KPI → Data

Decision → Question → KPI → Data must be treated as an explicit part of the analytical product, not as an undocumented implementation detail. Define the business purpose, population, time basis, owner, control and failure behaviour. Then connect the rule to evidence that can be reviewed when data, structures or stakeholder expectations change. In the context of design the hr datamart from decisions, not tables, this is what makes the outcome reusable, auditable and explainable.

02 · Deep dive

The data product contract

The data product contract must be treated as an explicit part of the analytical product, not as an undocumented implementation detail. Define the business purpose, population, time basis, owner, control and failure behaviour. Then connect the rule to evidence that can be reviewed when data, structures or stakeholder expectations change. In the context of design the hr datamart from decisions, not tables, this is what makes the outcome reusable, auditable and explainable.

Apply it

Document the rule, assign an owner, define a threshold or acceptance condition, and specify what users see when the control fails.

Decision takeaway

Make definitions, time, quality, ownership, access and failure behaviour visible. That is how a data pipeline becomes a trusted decision product.

Executive takeaway

What this means for workforce decision makers.

Good workforce architecture starts with the decisions leaders need to make, then works backward to data structures and controls. Data models should serve decision paths, not the other way around.

Key business questions

Questions leaders should ask next.

Which recurring decisions define the scope of the first HR DataMart release?

What entities and grain are required to answer those decisions reliably?

Which decisions need explainability before automation or scale?

Common mistakes

Failure patterns to avoid.

Mistake 1

Starting with copied source tables instead of decision journeys.

Mistake 2

Designing for every future use case before proving one high-value decision domain.

Mistake 3

Ignoring the questions executives will ask when a metric changes unexpectedly.

Practical implementation guidance

How to operationalize the idea.

  1. Document the decisions, consumers and action windows that matter most.
  2. Translate those needs into entity grain, dimensions, facts and control points.
  3. Use release planning that proves value through a narrow but trustworthy decision slice.
